A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHINE. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction/completion, QA, architecture-ablation, and scaling results, including Figure 5 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds long-context, multitask, architecture-ablation, and fine-tuning comparison results in Section 5.5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 5.5 introduces SHINE-R, a recurrent extension that processes context chunks sequentially. It generates separate adapters for updating the encoding of later chunks and for final inference, concatenating the saved adapters. This substantially extends the procedure beyond the retained SHINE architecture and objectives.

E1.justification: v2 adds LongBench long-context QA and summarization, including MultiFieldQA-English, Qasper, and QMSum. Appendix E.5 adds joint training and evaluation on DailyDialog, GSM8K, Persona-Chat, and SAMSum, extending coverage to conversational generation, mathematical reasoning, personalization, and summarization.

E2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds DoRA and IA3 as evaluated MS MARCO MQA comparators alongside the existing LoRA SFT approach. This expands the supplementary fine-tuning comparison; the original Naive, In-Context, Generative Adapter, and test-time-training comparison sets remain.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce SHINE-R training on contexts up to 18K tokens, joint multitask fine-tuning after MQA training, and SFT sweeps over 3/5/10 conversations and 5/10/20 epochs. Architecture studies add parameter-matched controls and further configurations. Table 11 explicitly applies SQuAD-style F1 to all four new tasks; original SHINE settings remain.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds linear-projection, final-layer-memory, and attention-design ablations; SFT budget sensitivity; context-quality/length analyses; and additional layer/rank scaling curves. These substantially expand tests of architectural choices and performance dependencies. The original coupled-attention 'Bitter Lesson' analysis is retained as E.1.

E5.justification: Figures 15–16 newly report fitted relationships and r coefficients between context characteristics and F1. The existing mean, median, and P10/P90 reporting in Figure 5 is retained. No additional seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–4 remain numerically unchanged, while v2 adds LongBench and multitask scores, SFT accuracy/runtime grids, and diagnostic curves. For example, the new 10-conversation/20-epoch settings yield 58.50 F1 for LoRA and 56.52 for DoRA. Table 11 reports GSM8K F1 of 25.27 for SHINE versus 44.48 for In-Context. These are additional results under newly reported settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and Appendix B/C complexity derivations are retained. Section 3.4 corrects R to the already-defined output dimension O in parameter slicing, a notation repair. SHINE-R is described procedurally without a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: expressive context-to-LoRA generation in one pass, reduced adaptation costs, strong task performance, and scaling potential. The added experiments and recurrent extension do not redefine those headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability discussion through explanations of the architecture ablations, insufficient training as a possible cause of SHINE-R's gap to In-Context, and missing reasoning-oriented training as an explanation for GSM8K performance. It also introduces interpretations linking context quality and length to adaptation success.

D1.justification: v2 supplies additional details such as linear-control depths and hidden size 8192, the supplementary conversation-generation/testing recipe, and joint multitask training. The code pointer changes from Yewei-Liu/SHINE to MuLabPKU/SHINE. Existing hardware, optimizer, base hyperparameters, and Appendix B data-processing instructions remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands research positioning through new discussions of test-time training, other architectures, and additional applications, with many added citations. Appendix C.7 adds a conceptual comparison with Drag-and-Drop LLMs. The Anonymous-to-Charakorn update for Doc-to-LoRA refers to the same existing work.

P1.justification: Most existing scientific prose and the overall narrative remain. Changes include localized grammar and notation corrections, front-matter updates, expanded related-work organization, new experimental subsections, and appendix reorganization: old Appendix D becomes E.1, while old Appendix E becomes D.

P2.justification: v2 adds the SHINE-R diagram, five analysis figures, the LongBench table, three SFT-grid tables, and the multitask table. These substantially expand the visual presentation. All original figure graphics are retained, with some relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Appendix E.2–E.3 substantially strengthens v1's limited empirical controls for architectural and efficiency claims through parameter-matched ablations and broader SFT method/budget comparisons, including settings where SFT wins on F1. Long-context and multitask evaluations also expose applicability limits. Sparse SHINE-R training details and a text-quality interpretation stronger than the near-zero correlations temper the gains, but the central validation is materially stronger.
